messages:
alex_cs: Drafting a short 'faststart' runbook we can share with customers for onboarding: focused, runnable, and minimal. PTAL before I send to Julia at Acme.

alex_cs: OVERVIEW:
- Objective: Get a customer from signup -> stable livemode with 95th pct latency < 350ms and predictable cost in 72 hours.
- Scope: caching, batching, streaming, quick validation, rollback steps, and a 15-min enablement agenda.

alex_cs: USER-FACING CHECKLIST (copy/paste to support email):
1) Enable lightweight prefix KV cache for repeated prompts (TTL default 300s).
2) Start with batching conservative window: max_wait_ms: 20, max_batch_size: 12.
3) Turn on streaming for interactive routes.
4) Run warmup traffic equal to 2x expected steady rps for 60s.
5) Confirm metrics in Console: route.latency.p95, route.cache.hit_rate, route.batch.size_avg, route.error.count.

alex_cs: EXAMPLE CONFIG (paste into customer YAML):
```yaml
route: /chat/complete
model: chat-xl
cache:
  prefix_kv: true
  ttl_seconds: 300
batching:
  latency_slo_ms: 350
  max_wait_ms: 20
  max_batch_size: 12
streaming:
  enabled: true
  chunk_size: 256
```

alex_cs: QUICK VALIDATION (run these and paste results back):
- Health: `curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .status`
- Warmup: `wrk -t2 -c16 -d60s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` (look at 95th pct latency)
- Console: verify cache hit_rate > 20% after warmup, batch.size_avg > 3 for background jobs.

kevin_eng: Add: telemetry keys also include `route.kv.prefetch_rate` for prefetch workflows and `route.kv.evictions` if TTLs are too short. For streaming, share a tiny node snippet.

kevin_eng: Streaming example:
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({model:'chat-xl', stream:true, prompt:'Hi'}),
});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
}
```

alex_cs: ROLLBACK & TROUBLESHOOT (customer-facing knobs):
- If latency spikes: set `max_wait_ms: 0` to disable batching.
- If outputs degrade after caching: set `prefix_kv: false`.
- If cost too high: route to `model_alias: acme-fallback-small` via Console routing.

alex_cs: RENEWAL/HEALTH SIGNALS (for CS to monitor first 7 days):
- Low usage (actual tokens < 30% expected) -> schedule AE check-in.
- >5% error rate or repeated manual rollbacks -> escalate to eng.
- Cache hit_rate < 10% after warmup -> advise prompt standardization.

tanya_csm: Suggest adding a 15-min enablement cadence: 0-5m metrics + Console, 5-10m change batch/cache and observe, 10-15m Qs & next steps. Also attach the one-liner warmup script.

alex_cs: Warmup one-liner (bash):
```bash
for i in {1..60}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"chat-xl","prompt":"warmup","max_tokens":10}'; sleep 0.5; done
```

sre-bot: deploy:faststart-runbook v0.9 saved to `customer-success/playbooks` by kevin_eng at 1999990001 :white_check_mark:

julia_acme: Thanks! A couple quick clarifications:
- Is 300s TTL safe for our login-related prompts?
- For warmup, do you recommend hitting different routes or the same one?

alex_cs: @julia_acme good q. For login prompts 300s is usually fine, drop to 60-120s if user metadata changes often. For warmup, hit common user-facing routes (login + search) to populate different caches.
